chief_complaint: severe eye pain, photophobia, and foreign body sensation after falling asleep wearing contact lenses (Pseudomonas Corneal Ulcer)
hpi_details: 22M college student presents to urgent eye clinic with 24 hours of severe right eye pain, redness, photophobia, excessive tearing, and thick yellowish discharge. Woke up unable to open his eye without severe stinging. Admits to sleeping overnight in his soft daily-wear contact lenses for the past 4 days without cleaning or disinfecting them.
ideas: in severe discomfort with eye squeezed shut, worried he scratched his eyeball
concerns: terrified of getting a permanent scar on his cornea that ruins his vision
expectations: wants antibiotic eye drops to kill the infection immediately

investigation_events.title: Emergency slit-lamp and fluorescein examination
investigation_events.availability_message: The slit-lamp and fluorescein findings are now available. Corneal scrapings have been sent, but intensive empiric topical antibiotics must not wait for final culture.

results.value: Central 2.5 x 2.5 mm dense stromal infiltrate with matching epithelial defect, surrounding edema, 2+ anterior chamber cells, and 1 mm hypopyon

clinical_knowledge.topic: Bacterial corneal ulcer (microbial keratitis), likely Pseudomonas evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Bacterial corneal ulcer (microbial keratitis), likely Pseudomonas is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes STAT ophthalmology emergency (Pseudomonas can enzymatically melt and perforate the cornea within 24-48 hours) with immediate cultures and intensive fortified topical antibiotic therapy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe eye pain, photophobia, and foreign body sensation after falling asleep wearing contact lenses (Pseudomonas Corneal Ulcer)

Key HPI features: 22M college student presents to urgent eye clinic with 24 hours of severe right eye pain, redness, photophobia, excessive tearing, and thick yellowish discharge. Woke up unable to open his eye without severe stinging. Admits to sleeping overnight in his soft daily-wear contact lenses for the past 4 days without cleaning or disinfecting them.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 78, Temp 36.9C. External exam shows diffuse conjunctival injection and thick mucopurulent discharge. Slit-lamp examination reveals a 2.5 x 2.5 mm round, dense, grayish-white stromal infiltrative ulcer located in the central cornea of the right eye with surrounding stromal edema. Fluorescein staining brightly highlights the overlying epithelial defect corresponding to the white stromal infiltrate. Anterior chamber shows 2+ cells with a 1 mm layer of white pus pooling at the bottom of the anterior chamber (hypopyon). Corneal scrapings obtained for Gram stain and culture (high concern for Pseudomonas aeruginosa).
Relevant background/PMH: Myopia, contact lens wearer
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Bacterial corneal ulcer (microbial keratitis), likely Pseudomonas.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Viral keratitis (HSV) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Hypopyon (pus layer in anterior chamber).
management_principles: STAT ophthalmology emergency (Pseudomonas can enzymatically melt and perforate the cornea within 24-48 hours) requiring immediate cultures and intensive fortified topical antibiotics
Immediately discontinue contact lens wear and discard old lenses/cases
Obtain corneal cultures and initiate intensive topical antibiotic therapy; use fortified antibiotics for large or vision-threatening ulcers as directed by ophthalmology
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 22M contact lens wearer presenting with acute painful red eye, purulence, and photophobia following overnight contact lens wear, suspicious for bacterial keratitis.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 78, Temp 36.9C. External exam shows diffuse conjunctival injection and thick mucopurulent discharge. Slit-lamp examination reveals a 2.5 x 2.5 mm round, dense, grayish-white stromal infiltrative ulcer located in the central cornea of the right eye with surrounding stromal edema. Fluorescein staining brightly highlights the overlying epithelial defect corresponding to the white stromal infiltrate. Anterior chamber shows 2+ cells with a 1 mm layer of white pus pooling at the bottom of the anterior chamber (hypopyon). Corneal scrapings obtained for Gram stain and culture (high concern for Pseudomonas aeruginosa).
reference_soap.assessment: Right Eye Severe Bacterial Corneal Ulcer (Microbial Keratitis) with Hypopyon, highly concerning for Pseudomonas aeruginosa secondary to contact lens abuse.
reference_soap.plan: STAT ophthalmology emergency: immediately discontinue contact lens wear and retain lenses/case for culture if requested. Obtain corneal scrapings for Gram stain and culture, then initiate intensive topical antibiotic therapy. For this central, vision-threatening ulcer, ophthalmology should direct fortified topical antibiotics (for example, fortified tobramycin plus cefazolin or vancomycin) at frequent intervals; commercial moxifloxacin 0.5% is not a fortified preparation. Use cycloplegia for ciliary-spasm pain as indicated. Do not start topical corticosteroids initially; they may be considered only by ophthalmology after 24-48 hours of effective antibacterial treatment when the organism is identified or clear clinical response is documented, and should be avoided when fungal, Acanthamoeba, or Nocardia infection is suspected.

learning_objectives: Recognize overnight contact lens wear as the single greatest risk factor for rapidly destructive Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacterial keratitis / corneal ulcers
Identify slit-lamp features of microbial keratitis (corneal epithelial defect over dense white/gray stromal infiltrate with hypopyon pooling in anterior chamber)

Explain why topical corticosteroids should not be started initially for microbial keratitis and may only be considered later by ophthalmology after effective antibacterial therapy and appropriate organism assessment
Outline intensive fortified topical antibiotic drop regimens (fluoroquinolones/tobramycin administered every 30-60 minutes around the clock)

teaching.diagnosis: Bacterial corneal ulcer (microbial keratitis), likely Pseudomonas
teaching.one_liner: 22M contact lens wearer who slept in his lenses for 4 days, now with severe pain, discharge, and a corneal ulcer with hypopyon.

must_ask.objective: Ask about contact lens hygiene practices
must_ask.say: Do you sleep in your contacts, and how often do you clean them?
What color and consistency is the discharge from your eye?

must_ask.objective: Assess pain severity and vision impact
must_ask.say: How severe is the pain, and has your vision gotten blurry?

must_ask.objective: Explain why lens wear must stop immediately
must_ask.say: Stop wearing contact lenses immediately. Keep the lenses and case if the eye specialist asks to culture them; otherwise, discard them.

must_ask.objective: Explain the intensive antibiotic drop schedule
must_ask.say: You'll need to use very strong antibiotic drops as often as every 30-60 minutes, even overnight.
